_comment: Harness guard hooks. Installed by bin/install-copilot.sh to
~/.copilot/hooks/harness-hooks.json with __COPILOT_HOME__ substituted.
This _comment key is documentation only; JSON has no comment syntax and
unknown keys are ignored. Delete it if your CLI version ever objects.
The 'bash' key is used rather than the generic 'command' key. A hook entry
takes mutually exclusive bash / powershell / command keys, and an explicit
per-platform key wins over the generic one, so naming 'bash' says exactly
what these scripts are.
WINDOWS GAP: v1 ships bash only. A Windows port adds a 'powershell' key
beside each 'bash' key below, pointing at a PowerShell 7+ twin of the same
script, like this:
{ "type": "command",
"bash": "__COPILOT_HOME__/hooks/block-destructive-bash.sh",
"powershell": "__COPILOT_HOME__/hooks/block-destructive-bash.ps1",
"timeoutSec": 10 }
No .ps1 twins exist yet, so on Windows these guards do not fire at all.
timeoutSec is 10. Do NOT lower it: a hook timeout FAILS OPEN, so a shorter
timeout makes a guard more likely to be skipped, not stricter.
The matchers below are honored by the CLI. VS Code parses them and then
ignores them, firing every hook on every tool call, so each script also
self-filters on tool_name. The matchers stay because the double filter
costs nothing and the CLI does use them.
